name: Taiwan
summary: Taiwan taxes individuals on Taiwan-source income at up to 40%. Foreign income, including foreign capital gains and dividends, is reached only by the 20% alternative minimum tax (income basic tax), which applies when foreign income is TWD 1 million or more and basic income exceeds TWD 7.5 million; for a family of this size that is close to a flat 20%. Taiwan listed-share gains are exempt (0.3% transaction tax), and Taiwan dividends cost up to 28%. Estate and gift tax (10%-20%) reaches only Taiwan-situs property of foreign nationals. There is no wealth tax and no US tax treaty.

regimes.name: Taiwan resident
regimes.description: Taiwan-source income at 5%-40%; foreign income only through the 20% income basic tax above TWD 7.5 million; estate tax on Taiwan assets only for foreigners.
regimes.eligibility: Foreigners are resident if present 183 days or more in a calendar year.

capital_gains.summary: Taiwan taxes individuals' Taiwan-source income at 5%-40%. Gains on Taiwan securities are exempt from income tax (a 0.3% securities transaction tax applies to share sales). Foreign-source income, including gains on foreign securities and foreign property, is outside the regular income tax but enters the alternative minimum tax (income basic tax, IBT) at 20% once a resident's foreign income is TWD 1 million or more and basic income exceeds TWD 7.5 million, with a credit for foreign tax. Taiwan real estate acquired from 2016 is under the consolidated house and land income tax: 45% (2 years or less), 35% (2-5), 20% (5-10), 15% (over 10 years); a self-used home qualifies for TWD 4 million exemption and 10% above it.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: IBT: the household deducts TWD 7.5 million once from its basic income and pays 20% of the rest (Income Basic Tax Act art. 13, whose text says TWD 6 million, raised to 7.5 million by the Ministry of Finance's CPI adjustment under art. 3(2); amount confirmed on the Ministry of Finance portal, updated 2026-04-15). A household's foreign income under TWD 1 million is left out entirely; at TWD 1 million or more all of it counts (art. 12). The art. 3(2) adjustment applies when the CPI has risen 10% or more since the last adjustment, in TWD 100,000 steps.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: IBT is payable only to the extent it exceeds regular income tax. For the family's scale (foreign income far above TWD 7.5 million) the effective rate approaches 20%. Gains on certain unlisted/privately placed securities are IBT add-back items.

open_questions: Treatment of gains on unlisted Taiwan shares under IBT not verified.
The 2026 IBT deduction of TWD 7.5 million was confirmed from the Ministry of Finance portal text (updated 2026-04-15), not from a 2026 announcement.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Foreign gains: 20% IBT. Domestic listed: income-tax exempt, 0.3% securities transaction tax on proceeds = 0.6% of the gain assuming the gain is half the proceeds. Private business sale (unlisted Taiwan company): assumed to fall into IBT at 20% (low confidence). Local real estate held over 10 years: 15%. Headline 45% = short-holding house and land rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Securities gains remain exempt even for frequent traders (general knowledge); property dealing businesses are taxed under the house and land rules.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: House and land tax rates fall with holding period (above).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign income is taxed only through IBT (20%) and only for residents (183 days or domiciled).

dividends.summary: Taiwan dividends of resident individuals are either included in consolidated income (up to 40%) with an 8.5% credit capped at TWD 80,000, or taxed separately at 28%. Foreign dividends are foreign-source income, outside regular tax but included in IBT at 20% (same thresholds as above) with credit for foreign tax.
dividends.important_exceptions: Dividend options of Income Tax Act art. 15: an 8.5% credit capped at TWD 80,000 per return on consolidated income, or a separate flat 28% (English text of the Act opened 2026-10-16).

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: separate 28% option (better than 40% less the capped credit for large dividends). Foreign: 20% IBT before credit; US 30% WHT (no treaty) would fully absorb it.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 21% WHT on dividends to non-residents, reducible by treaty (corporate summary, not opened).
dividends.treaty_network: About 35 comprehensive agreements; no income tax treaty with the US (the 2025 US legislation to extend treaty benefits was not verified as in force).
dividends.holding_company_notes: CIT 20% plus 5% profit retention tax on undistributed earnings.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Land value tax 1%-5.5% of assessed land value (lower rate for owner-occupied residences, not verified) and house tax 1%-4.8% of assessed value for non-commercial buildings (PwC); luxury tax 10% on certain goods.

inheritance.summary: Estate tax applies to the estate (estate basis) at 10% up to TWD 56.21 million, 15% to TWD 112.42 million and 20% above (CPI-adjusted amounts, unchanged for 2026), after an exemption of TWD 13.33 million (Estate and Gift Tax Act art. 13, 18). For non-ROC nationals, and ROC nationals without habitual residence, only property located in Taiwan is taxed (arts. 1 and 3), and the deductions for a spouse, children, parents and others do not apply to them (art. 17, last paragraph); only the exemption does. Gift tax: 10%-20% after a TWD 2.44 million annual exemption per donor, same scope rule.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Estate exemption TWD 13.33 million per decedent, also for non-ROC nationals (art. 18). The family and other deductions (spouse TWD 5.53 million, TWD 560,000 per lineal descendant, parents, funeral) are for ROC nationals habitually resident in Taiwan only; art. 17 disapplies items 1-7 for non-ROC nationals and limits the funeral and debt deductions to Taiwan. Gift: TWD 2.44 million per donor per year.
inheritance.important_exceptions: A foreign family pays estate tax only on Taiwan-situs assets (e.g. a Taiwan home and Taiwan shares). ROC nationals are taxed worldwide if domiciled in Taiwan within two years before death or resident more than 365 days in those two years (Art. 4).

inheritance.spouse_note: For a decedent who is a non-ROC national or an ROC national living abroad, the spouse deduction (TWD 5.53 million for ROC residents) and the other family deductions of art. 17 items 1-7 do not apply (art. 17, last paragraph); the spouse is taxed like any other heir on Taiwan-situs property. Gifts between spouses are exempt, but gifts within two years of death are added back (art. 15).
inheritance.gift_tax: Gift tax 10% to TWD 28.11 million, 15% to 56.21 million, 20% above, after TWD 2.44 million per donor per year; non-nationals only on gifts of Taiwan property.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Nationality plus habitual residence (Art. 4): ROC nationals with a domicile in the two prior years or 365+ days of stay are taxed worldwide; non-nationals are always taxed on Taiwan property only. Amounts are indexed by law: art. 12-1 raises the exemption, bracket limits and deductions when the CPI has risen 10% or more since the last adjustment, from the following year, and the Ministry of Finance announces them each December (2026 amounts unchanged).

residency.tax_residency_test: Foreign individuals: resident if present 183 days or more in a calendar year. ROC nationals with household registration are resident if domiciled and habitually residing, unless the 31-day rule applies.

routes.name: Investment-based resident certificate (ARC), Employment Gold Card, APRC
routes.requirements: Residence through investment in a Taiwan business, employment, or the Employment Gold Card for professionals; permanent residence (APRC) after qualifying years or for major investors (thresholds not verified).

corporate.summary: 20% CIT (income up to TWD 120,000 exempt); 5% profit retention tax on undistributed earnings; 12% corporate IBT, with proposals to raise it to 15% for Pillar Two groups.

homicide_rate.notes: 158 intentional homicide (故意殺人, 'murder') offences known to the police in 2025, divided by 23.35 million population implied by Table 1 (608,717 criminal cases at 2,606.96 per 100,000). Counts offences, not victims, and Taiwan's category may include attempted murder, so it is not exactly the UNODC victim-based definition (2024: 136 offences, about 0.58).

us_citizen_notes: No US-Taiwan income tax treaty in force (to the extent checked); US citizens credit Taiwan IBT against US tax on the same income. Taiwan estate tax on Taiwan assets is creditable against US estate tax within limits.
